lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use the single project Feijoa concept to teach opposite entire gland-dotted leaves with an intramarginal vein, many conspicuous stamens, inferior ovary and fleshy berry, while clearly marking it as a nonlocal cultivated comparison.

project_scope.note: The current project pool contains Feijoa sellowiana. Current Kew accepts Feijoa sellowiana and treats Acca sellowiana as a synonym. Its native range is southern Brazil to northeastern Argentina/Uruguay; it is not a Central Texas native anchor.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with a leaf held to light: look for pellucid oil-gland dots and an intramarginal vein running just inside the leaf edge. In flower, confirm many conspicuous stamens surrounding a single style above an inferior ovary.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Woody shrubs or trees; leaves simple, entire, exstipulate and commonly opposite. Pellucid gland dots and an intramarginal collecting vein are strong family clues.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually 4–5-merous with a well-developed hypanthium and usually numerous stamens. Ovary commonly inferior or semi-inferior with a single style.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Capsule, berry or drupe across the family. Feijoa produces a fleshy green berry with many seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: For this project: woody + opposite entire gland-dotted leaves + intramarginal vein + many stamens + inferior ovary = Myrtaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: leaf oil glands → intramarginal vein → many stamens → inferior ovary → Feijoa fruit → Myrtales comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Myrtaceae gives the learner a powerful leaf-plus-flower combination: translucent oil glands and a near-edge vein on the leaf, then a flower dominated by a brush of stamens.

steps.title: 1 · Backlight the oil glands
steps.look_for: Small pellucid translucent dots scattered through the blade.
steps.why_it_matters: A high-value family clue that separates Myrtaceae from many opposite-leaved woody families.

steps.title: 2 · Trace the intramarginal vein
steps.look_for: A collecting vein running roughly parallel to the margin just inside the leaf edge.
steps.why_it_matters: Pairs with the oil glands to make the vegetative family door much stronger.

steps.title: 3 · Count 'many' stamens
steps.look_for: A conspicuous brush of long red/crimson stamens with yellow anthers surrounding the style.
steps.why_it_matters: The androecium is far more diagnostic than flower color or petal shape alone.

steps.title: 4 · Locate the inferior ovary
steps.look_for: Petals and stamens arise above an ovary embedded below the flower.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects Myrtaceae to Myrtales while separating it from project Lythraceae's usually superior ovary.

steps.title: 5 · Feijoa whole-plant door
steps.look_for: Opposite leathery leaves, dark glossy upper surface, densely pale/white-tomentose underside, showy many-stamen flower and oblong green berry.
steps.why_it_matters: A compact genus/species recognition card for the only project Myrtaceae taxon.

steps.title: 6 · Mark it as nonlocal
steps.look_for: Feijoa sellowiana is South American in origin; project use is ornamental/comparison rather than Central Texas native anchor.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents family recognition from accidentally becoming a native-plant recommendation.

comparisons.title: Myrtaceae vs Lythraceae
comparisons.rule: Myrtaceae project plant is woody, gland-dotted, intramarginal-veined, many-stamened and inferior-ovaried. Lythraceae project plants are wetland herbs with a persistent floral tube and usually superior ovary.

comparisons.title: Myrtaceae vs Onagraceae
comparisons.rule: Both commonly have inferior ovaries in Myrtales, but Onagraceae project plants are herbs with a much smaller fixed stamen set and often a 4-lobed stigma; Myrtaceae is woody with oil glands, intramarginal veins and many stamens.

comparisons.title: Myrtaceae vs Rutaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can show pellucid oil glands. Project Myrtaceae has opposite simple leaves, many stamens and an inferior ovary; project Rutaceae has mostly alternate leaves, fewer stamens, a floral disk and a superior ovary.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not use aroma by crushing as a required crew test; backlit gland dots, intramarginal venation and reproductive characters are safer. Family-level Myrtaceae is diverse, so the module intentionally centers on the single project Feijoa concept.

genera.fast_cue: opposite leathery gland-dotted leaves + white-tomentose underside + many red stamens + green berry

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Current Kew treats Acca sellowiana as a homotypic synonym; retain Acca as searchable provenance only.
